children: , the global payments network, pushed deeper into AI-driven commerce by backing common identity standards for autonomous shopping agents, Reuters reported. The shares slipped approximately 0.5% to $570.60 Wednesday. The bigger story is not simply whether AI can shop for consumersit is whether payment networks can reliably identify which software agents are actually authorized to spend their money.

Mastercard, Visa and Ant International are developing a Know-Your-Agent framework designed to verify approved purchasing agents across card networks, digital wallets, marketplaces and AI platforms. Each participant would still control its own authorization and risk policies, but a shared identity layer could eliminate the need for merchants and AI developers to build separate verification systems for every payment ecosystem. That matters because fewer integration hurdles could make agent-based payments easier to deploy at scale.

Mastercard expects more than one in ten online shoppers to routinely let AI agents make purchases for them by 2030, while its Agent Pay for Machines initiative already has more than 30 supporters, including Stripe, Coinbase and Cloudflare. The valuation picture adds another angle: the chart shows Mastercard at $570.60 versus a GF Value estimate of $682.45, putting the shares 16.39% below that benchmark. That discount suggests the market is assigning limited value today to Mastercard's longer-term agentic-commerce opportunity, leaving executionrather than the AI narrative itselfas the key question for investors.

title: Mastercard Slips as AI Payments Trade Exclusivity for Scale
